key_insight: Vision–language reasoning failures often arise from a reporting bias in caption-style training data: people omit tacit facts, and increasing model scale alone does not teach models to recover those unreported details.
problem_solved: Identifies and isolates reporting bias in VLM training data as a root cause of poor explicit reasoning, explaining why larger models still fail on tasks that require facts typically left unstated in captions.
method: Quantitative analysis of caption corpora underlying popular VLMs (e.g., OpenCLIP) to measure how frequently visually verifiable facts are omitted.
Design of probing tasks/benchmarks that require explicit reasoning about tacit visual facts and evaluation of VLM performance across model scales.
Ablations showing the relative effects of scaling versus changes to supervision (data augmentation or targeted labeling) on reasoning performance.
impact: Shows practitioners that improving VLM reasoning requires addressing dataset pragmatics and supervision strategies, not just scaling models—guiding dataset curation, annotation, and training choices for reliable multimodal reasoning.
visual_elements: Bar chart: frequency of omitted/tacit facts in caption corpora (e.g., count of verifiable facts mentioned vs omitted).
Line plot: reasoning task accuracy vs model scale, highlighting plateau where scaling no longer improves performance.
Side-by-side examples: real caption vs image with the missing tacit fact annotated (what humans omit vs what a reasoning task requires).
Flow diagram: cause → reporting bias in captions → missing supervision for tacit facts → VLM reasoning failure, plus interventions (targeted labels, synthetic captions).
paper_title: Scale Can't Overcome Pragmatics: The Impact of Reporting Bias on Vision-Language Reasoning
paper_authors: Amita Kamath, Jack Hessel, Khyathi Chandu, Jena D. Hwang, Kai-Wei Chang
